Title: Wall Street's performance isn't so 'exceptional' on the global stage
Article:
ORLANDO: As the S&P 500 and Dow roar to new highs, with the Nasdaq not far behind, attention is understandably centred on the resilience of corporate America and its extraordinary earnings power.
But from a global perspective, the performance of Wall Street – and the US – is far from exceptional. So far this year, the S&P 500 and Dow are up 12 per cent, and the Nasdaq is up 14 per cent.
That's not too shabby, especially after last year's bumper gains.
Moreover, sky-high earnings growth is no longer isolated to the US tech sector, with consumer discretionary companies and materials also posting eye-watering numbers.
Yet the big US indices are barely outperforming many of their developed market peers, and, in certain instances, they are lagging.
Benchmark equity indices in the UK, Europe, and Canada have all recently hit fresh peaks, clocking year-to-date gains of 10 per cent, 12 per cent and 12 per cent, respectively.
Asian markets have been highly volatile, recording sharp drops in July, but Japanese equities continue to outperform Wall Street, with the Nikkei up 28 per cent since January 1.
And that's despite the country's recent currency and bond market ructions. Perhaps the "American exceptionalism" mindset is just hard to shake, but when looking at economic growth and earnings – two of the most important foundations for a robust stock market – the US simply isn't outgunning its rivals to the extent that narrative might suggest.
MIND THE GAP
US earnings growth forecasts for the second quarter and calendar year 2026 are impressive. Year-on-year aggregate S&P 500 earnings growth forecasts for calendar year 2026 are running at a punchy 30 per cent, before slowing to a still respectable 15 per cent next year, according to LSEG's Tajinder Dhillon.
But other regions are also enjoying earnings booms – and not just AI-frenzied emerging markets like South Korea and Taiwan. In Europe, UBS equity strategists predict 25 per cent earnings growth this year and next, driven by a cyclical recovery and large-scale structural investment in areas such as AI, electrification, and defence.
The gap between the US and European economies also isn't as wide as many would guess.
While the US looks quite healthy – perhaps too healthy – on a nominal basis, headwinds are gathering force, namely high real yields, sticky inflation, and policy credibility issues.
Real GDP growth over the last few years has been on a clear downward path, to a 1.5 per cent annualised pace in the second quarter of this year from almost 3.0 per cent in 2023.
Meanwhile, the euro zone – often knocked as less dynamic than the all-powerful American juggernaut – grew 1.6 per cent in the second quarter, slightly outpacing the US.
Citi's economic surprise indexes measure actual data prints relative to consensus forecasts, and the euro zone's is currently the highest in 3 1/2 years, while the US' is the lowest in three months.
In developed Asia, the relative attractiveness versus Wall Street looks a little less clear-cut. Japan's robust equity performance this year comes with caveats, not least that the Nikkei slumped 8.0 per cent last month.
Japan has plenty of headwinds too, including a weak currency and policy credibility issues on both the fiscal and monetary fronts. Yet Citi's Japan economic surprise index this week soared to its highest level in five years, although a stronger yen and elevated bond yields might soon cap that. Finally, there's the issue of relative rates.
Equity investors like low real interest rates, and they're getting that in the US, where the Federal Reserve's inflation-adjusted policy rate is around zero. But real rates in the euro zone and Japan are even lower, both around minus 0.7 per cent.
'MARKET PURGATORY'
To be fair, US multinationals aren't getting the boost from a weaker dollar that they got last year. But neither are they suffering from a strong dollar — the greenback is flat against a basket of major G10 currencies so far this year, despite all the noise around its recent 40-year high against the Japanese yen.
Exchange rates don't appear to be an issue for corporate earnings in 2026.
None of this is to say Wall Street won't continue to break new highs for the rest of this year and beyond. Nor is anyone suggesting investors are about to withdraw from US markets, home to the world's most productive and profitable companies.
Indeed, foreign demand for U.S. equities has never been higher, suggesting "FOMO" — the fear of missing out — is alive and well.
But in investing, it's all about relative value. And other markets around the world seem just as attractive right now, maybe even more so.
That's partly a matter of price. On a forward 12-month price/earnings basis, the US is still significantly more expensive than Europe and the UK, although more comparable to Japan.
Up until now, Wall Street's multiples have been justified by earnings. But for how much longer?
Much depends on what happens with AI. Wall Street's rally over the past year has been largely driven by AI investment, which will total almost $600 billion in the US alone this year, according to Goldman Sachs estimates.
But it's fair to assume that these expectations are already "in the price" of US stocks, so the question is whether these gargantuan outlays can continue.
"We may be reaching a pinnacle of sorts in earnings and economic momentum, and investors are struggling with what comes next," says Callie Cox, chief market strategist at Ritholtz Wealth. "We're in market purgatory, and this may still be a good time to be strategic about where value lies."

Title: DVS: Rocky the dog death probe referred to DPP
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The investigation papers into the death of a dog in Klang, which recently sparked public attention, have been submitted to the Deputy Public Prosecutor (DPP) for review.
The Selangor Department of Veterinary Services (DVS) said the investigation papers were referred to the DPP's office yesterday together with several recommendations based on the findings of the probe.
It said further action would be taken after receiving instructions from the DPP.
"The department urges the public to remain calm and allow the authorities to carry out their duties in accordance with the legal process," it said in a statement yesterday.
The department also gave its assurance that the investigation had been conducted fairly, transparently and without influence from opinions or statements made by unrelated parties.
It said the investigation was based solely on the available facts and evidence, in accordance with existing legal provisions.
On Aug 2, the department lodged a
police report
and recorded statements from several people as part of its investigation into the alleged abuse of Rocky the dog, which was captured in a video.
The DVS said its Animal Welfare Team filed the report after receiving the carcass of a male dog, following the circulation of a video showing several individuals tying and pulling the dog by its neck while a woman pleaded for it to be released.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: US refunds US$100bil in tariffs struck down by Supreme Court
Article:
WASHINGTON: President Donald Trump's administration has refunded about US$100 billion from tariffs that it collected before the US Supreme Court struck down those duties, a court filing showed.
DETAILS:
* The court filing in the US Court of International Trade said that "refunds (duties plus interest) of approximately US$100 billion have been completed using the Consolidated Administration and Processing of Entries Refund component, certified by the agency, and sent to the U.S. Department of Treasury for disbursement."
* The amount as of the end of July was noted in Tuesday's filing by US customs officials.
* It represented more than half of the US$166 billion collected in tariffs that the Supreme Court struck down in February.
* Trump has made tariffs ​a central pillar of his foreign and trade policies despite criticism from some analysts and legal setbacks.
* Critics have complained that the refunds have not reached households but have instead gone to corporate importers.
* "Trump is sending the 'refunds' to the companies, not working people. Every single cent of these refunds should go back to American consumers," Democratic Congressman Greg Casar said this week.
* The Supreme Court ruled against most of Trump's widest-ranging tariffs on February 20, finding that the International Emergency Economic Powers Act (IEEPA) does not authorise the president to unilaterally impose tariffs on goods imported from trading partners.
* Trump responded to that ruling by escalating his trade campaign, calling Supreme Court justices "disloyal" and issuing new temporary 10% tariffs under a different legal authority that, like IEEPA, no president had previously used to impose tariffs.
* The president then issued another round of global tariffs imposed under Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974, which is meant to combat unfair or discriminatory economic practices by other nations.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Ringgit opens slightly higher as soft us data weighs on greenback
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit opened slightly higher against the US dollar on Thursday, supported by improved market sentiment after weaker-than-expected United States (US) economic data weighed on the greenback.
At 8 am, the local currency strengthened marginally to 4.0905/0960 against the greenback from Wednesday's close of 4.0920/0960.
Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said softer-than-expected US economic data had pushed the US Dollar Index (DXY) down 0.18 per cent to 99.676.
"The Automatic Data Processing (ADP) Nonfarm Employment Change came in at 44,000 in July, below the consensus estimate of 68,000 and down from 95,000 in June.
"The US Institute for Supply Management (ISM) non-manufacturing index stood at 54.1 in July, below the consensus estimate of 54.5," he told Bernama.
Mohd Afzanizam said US Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook had indicated she would support an interest rate hike if inflation remained persistently high.
"In addition, the potential reopening of the Strait of Hormuz has kept Brent crude prices below US$80 per barrel. As such, the US dollar/ringgit pair is expected to trade between RM4.07 and RM4.09 today," he said.
Meanwhile, Quintex Intel global strategist Stephen Innes said the broader US dollar was slightly weaker in early trade, although risk sentiment had softened as investors awaited final details of a potential West Asia peace deal.
"Markets are also entering the 48-hour window ahead of the US non-farm payrolls report, prompting traders to rebalance risk and reduce exposure.
"This suggests the ringgit may remain confined to a relatively narrow trading range in the early hours," he added.
The ringgit, however, traded mostly lower against a basket of major currencies at the open.
It eased against the Japanese yen to 2.5942/5978 from 2.5940/5967 at Wednesday's close and slipped against the euro to 4.7266/7329 from 4.7222/7268, but strengthened against the British pound to 5.5087/5161 from 5.5107/5161.
Against regional currencies, the ringgit traded mixed.
It weakened against the Singapore dollar to 3.1932/1978 from 3.1916/1950 and fell against the Thai baht to 12.3655/3881 from 12.3216/3381.
However, the local currency edged up against the Indonesian rupiah to 228.0/228.5 from 228.1/228.5 and was unchanged against the Philippine peso at 6.73/6.74.

Title: RM3.03bil Penang Mutiara LRT systems contract awarded to MRCB-Theta Edge JV
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: Mass Rapid Transit Corporation Sdn Bhd (MRT Corp) has awarded the RM3.03 billion system turnkey contract for the Mutiara Line Light Rail Transit (LRT) project to a joint venture between Malaysian Resources Corporation Bhd (MRCB) and Theta Edge Bhd.
The award marks a key milestone in delivering Penang's first metro rail system, allowing railway systems design and integration to proceed alongside ongoing civil works.
The contract covers seven core packages: rolling stock and depot equipment, signalling and train control, trackwork, power supply, railway supervisory control and data acquisition (SCADA), telecommunications and information technology systems, and automatic fare collection.
The 29km project remains on track for completion in December 2031.
Construction of the Mutiara Line is gaining momentum, with 45 pile caps and 32 pier columns completed. Works are underway across 14 of the 19 sections under Civil Main Contract 1 (CMC1), which covers the alignment from Silicon Island to Komtar.
"We have adopted a parallel design-and-build approach by issuing construction reference drawings while detailed engineering designs are being finalised, allowing works to progress without waiting for the completion of the entire design package," MRT Corp said in a statement.
Detailed construction drawings for CMC1 cover major infrastructure components including pile caps, piers, viaducts, and stations. Land acquisition for the package has reached 93 per cent following cooperation between the federal government, state government, and relevant agencies.
Soil investigation works have started at Silicon Island for the future project depot, while site clearing at Tapak Pesta was completed following its handover by the state government in April.
Meanwhile, tender evaluation for Civil Main Contract 2 (CMC2) — covering the extension from Komtar to Penang Sentral — is ongoing, with the contract expected to be awarded in November.
Bumiputera participation under CMC1 has exceeded 20 per cent of the total contract value through subcontract awards as construction expands.
MRT Corp thanked Penang residents for their patience and cooperation, reaffirming its commitment to minimising disruptions while delivering the state's first metro rail system.

Title: Heritage building collapse raises safety concerns at Lebuh Armenian
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: Shock and concern gripped traders and visitors  in Lebuh Armenian after  a heritage building facade collapsed on Tuesday, injuring two Sri Lankan tourists  and raising  questions about  the safety of ageing structures in the Unesco World Heritage Site.
The incident, which occurred about 1pm on one of Penang's busiest tourist streets, left business operators worried that public confidence could be shaken if similar incidents recur.
Souvenir shop operator Teoh Guat Choo, who has been running her business  for about 20 years, said the collapse was alarming given the large crowds.
"We hope everyone involved is safe. This area is always packed with visitors."
[[nid:1505076]]
She said the nearby Cheah Kongsi conducted inspections of its heritage building several times a year.
Another trader, who identified herself only as Stella, said the collapse highlighted the urgent need for continuous monitoring of ageing heritage buildings.
"This is one of Penang's top tourist attractions. Safety must come first because incidents like this can frighten visitors away," she said, adding that part of the wall of her shop  chipped just last week due to wear and tear.
Visitor Dini Irsalina Azran, 26, from Selangor, urged authorities to intensify inspections before another tragedy occurred.
"If these buildings are not  maintained, their condition will deteriorate."
Raihana Ahmad Shahir, 23, from Seberang Prai, said she would continue visiting the  enclave, but stressed that  authorities and building owners must ensure the buildings were  safe.
The injured woman remains warded at Penang Hospital. One man was discharged.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: BN stays out of DAP's cabinet vote, calls it party matter
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Barisan Nasional  has described DAP's upcoming national congress, where delegates will vote on whether the party should remain in the unity government, as an internal party matter.
Senior BN leaders declined to speculate on the outcome of the Aug 16 vote or its implications following DAP's poor showing in the Sabah, Johor and Negri Sembilan elections.
BN secretary-general Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abdul Kadir said it was up to DAP to decide its direction, dismissing suggestions that the vote reflected instability in the unity government.
Asked if DAP's possible withdrawal from the cabinet would lead to a reshuffle, Zambry said it was premature to speculate on the matter.
[[nid:1505072]]
"Any decision on the composition of the cabinet is the prime minister's prerogative under the Constitution and should be based on the needs of national administration and government stability."
On calls for an early general election if DAP quits the government, Zambry said BN remained committed to political stability and continuity.
"A general election should not be the first option whenever political differences arise within any party."
He reiterated BN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi's position that the coalition remained committed to the unity government until Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim dissolves Parliament.
BN vice-president Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin also declined to comment on the matter.
"Let's wait until after the congress. Why should we interfere in another party's affairs?"
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Salmonella outbreak linked to Mexican jalapenos sickens 345 across 27 US states
Article:
WASHINGTON: The US CDC and the FDA said on Wednesday they are investigating a multistate Salmonella outbreak linked to jalapeno peppers from Mexico, which have sickened 345 people across 27 states and prompted a recall of affected products.
The FDA said 36 hospitalisations and no deaths have been reported, while the investigation remains ongoing.
The health agencies linked the outbreak to jalapeno peppers supplied by a common grower in Sinaloa and distributed in the US by Coast Citrus Distributors.
The company has agreed to recall the remaining product and is notifying affected customers, the FDA said.
The US investigation identified restaurants including Chipotle Mexican Grill and QDOBA, a Mexican-style restaurant chain, as recipients of jalapenos imported by Coast Citrus Distributors.
Chipotle has since switched jalapeno suppliers for its restaurants beginning July 20, while QDOBA stopped using jalapenos on July 28 and is no longer serving them, according to the FDA.
"FDA does not consider there to be a current ongoing risk from these establishments to consumers in this outbreak," the Food and Drug Administration said in a statement. — REUTERS
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: DAP's Aug 16 vote a test of Anwar's unity government [WATCH]
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Political observers believe DAP's Aug 16 national congress will be  a defining moment for the party and the unity government, as delegates will vote by secret ballot whether DAP should remain in the government until the end of the parliamentary term or withdraw.
The motion follows  DAP's poor showing in the Sabah, Johor and Negri Sembilan elections. More than 4,000 delegates are expected to determine whether the party's ministers and deputy ministers should remain in the cabinet.
Political analyst and former  member of parliament Ong Kian Ming said the vote was essentially   a referendum on Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's leadership.
[[nid:1505102]]
"A vote for DAP ministers and deputy ministers to resign is effectively a vote of no confidence in Anwar and what he has failed to deliver in terms of political reforms over the past four years."
Ong, who was a DAP  Central Executive Committee member,  warned that the government could collapse if Barisan Nasional or Umno also withdrew their ministers, leaving Anwar with little choice but to dissolve Parliament and call the 16th General Election.
DAP vice-chairman and Bangi MP Syahredzan Johan said the vote was essentially about whether DAP's ministers should remain in office, adding that the party would continue supporting Anwar as prime minister until the end of the parliamentary term.
He acknowledged that a withdrawal from the cabinet would create political "tremors", adding that less committed coalition partners might use it as a reason to withdraw their support.
"The tremors could remain aftershocks or become a political earthquake."
On the ground, DAP delegates in Penang appear to favour remaining in the unity government, arguing that stability and ongoing reforms outweighed calls to leave.
Several delegates who spoke on condition of anonymity said DAP should not abandon reforms midway despite frustrations over recent election setbacks.
One delegate said leaving the cabinet would risk creating a political vacuum that could benefit the opposition, particularly Pas, while jeopardising policy gains achieved through DAP's participation in government.
"Malaysia   experienced   political instability from 2020 to 2022. We should not risk returning to that."
Another delegate said withdrawing from the government now would only reinforce the opposition's narrative that DAP was a source of political instability.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Tabung Haji RCI: Azeez says report did not mention his name
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Former Tabung Haji  chairman Datuk Seri Abdul Azeez Abdul Rahim has brushed aside Bersatu's call for him to confirm whether he had been contacted by the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) over the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report into the pilgrim fund.
"The RCI report did not mention any of our names," he told the
New Straits Times
.
Azeez was responding to Bersatu supreme council member Dr Afif Bahardin, who had urged Azeez to disclose a letter he claimed to possess from former MACC chief commissioner Tan Sri Azam Baki, dated 2021, which purportedly cleared him of any wrongdoing in relation to the fund's management.
Azeez, who chaired Tabung Haji from 2013 to 2018, had previously said he was prepared to be investigated again if necessary, while maintaining that  MACC had already cleared him.
He reiterated that he served only as a non-executive chairman and had no authority to approve transactions or investments on his own.
Azeez also said the more than 200-page RCI report contained no evidence that depositors' funds had been misappropriated, contrary to previous allegations.
Afif also called on Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki to step aside as Majlis Amanah Rakyat chairman until investigations into the RCI findings were concluded to avoid any perception of interference.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Drug arrests raise fears of syndicates recruiting Malaysians [WATCH]
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The recent  arrests of Malaysians in Indonesia, Singapore and Thailand over drug smuggling attempts could signal a broader recruitment drive by transnational drug syndicates targeting vulnerable Malaysians, said a crime watchdog.
Malaysians Against Rape, Assault and Snatch Theft founder Dave Avran said the string of cases should not be viewed as isolated incidents but possible indicators of organised criminal networks exploiting Malaysians as disposable drug couriers.
"Something very ugly is developing around Malaysia's borders and pretending these are merely isolated cases of a few Malaysians making spectacularly stupid life choices is no longer good enough.
"This is not a drug problem anymore. This is a recruitment problem. Increasingly, it looks like Malaysia is being mined for people willing to become the disposable workforce of international drug syndicates," he told the
New Straits Times
.
His remarks came after a series of high-profile arrests involving Malaysians recently.
Among them was a Malaysia Airlines pilot arrested in Jakarta late last month after Indonesian authorities caught him with more than 70,000 ecstasy tablets, together with methamphetamine.
On Monday, another Malaysian, a 22-year-old from Johor, was arrested at Juanda International Airport in Surabaya after authorities  discovered 990g of methamphetamine and 1,089 ecstasy tablets concealed beneath a corset strapped to his body.
In Singapore, a Malaysian was arrested at the Woodlands checkpoint  on Aug 1 after authorities seized about 9kg of cannabis and 530g of methamphetamine hidden inside his vehicle.
In Thailand, three Malaysian men were arrested at Hat Yai Railway Station on July 31 after attempting to smuggle 87kg of methamphetamine concealed in three suitcases. Thai authorities said the syndicate had promised to pay the trio the equivalent of about RM24,000.
Avran said the diversity of those allegedly recruited suggested syndicates were no longer relying on traditional drug couriers.
"The pilot isn't the stereotypical drug mule. Then look at the 22-year-old arrested in Surabaya. Financial problems. Debt. An international syndicate. A comparatively easy way to make money.
"The syndicates are recruiting people from different walks of life. They don't particularly care who you are. They care whether you are useful, vulnerable and disposable. That should frighten us," he said.
Avran said Malaysia's strategic location made it attractive to international trafficking networks, with routes linking Thailand, Singapore and Indonesia providing multiple avenues for moving illicit drugs.
"We know about these mules because they were caught. What about the ones who weren't? Every arrested courier is a potential doorway into an international trafficking organisation," he said.
He urged authorities to treat such arrests not only as narcotics cases but also as border security matters requiring greater intelligence-sharing between police, Customs, the Immigration Department, the National Anti-Drugs Agency  and their regional counterparts.
He said investigators should focus on identifying those who recruited and supplied the drugs in Malaysia, as well as the syndicates receiving them overseas.
At the same time, he said Malaysians arrested abroad remained innocent until proven guilty in court.
"We should not assume that every Malaysian arrested overseas is necessarily guilty. Allegations must still be proven in court.
"But when multiple Malaysians are being arrested in Indonesia, Singapore and Thailand within days, carrying substantial quantities of dangerous drugs, it is perfectly legitimate to ask whether we are witnessing something larger than coincidence.
"The question is why are international drug syndicates finding Malaysians so easy to recruit?"
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Myanmar president visits Thailand on quest for legitimacy as Bangkok backs engagement
Article:
BANGKOK: Myanmar's junta chief turned President Min Aung Hlaing will make an official visit to Thailand on Thursday, as Bangkok makes a push for re-engagement between its war-torn neighbour and the regional bloc Asean.
Myanmar's leaders have been barred from summits of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations since 2021, when Min Aung Hlaing staged a coup against the elected government of Nobel laureate Aung San Suu Kyi that led to a civil war that has killed an estimated 100,000 people.
The retired general is the subject of a raft of Western sanctions and has been seeking international legitimacy since becoming Myanmar's president in April, which followed an election won overwhelmingly by an army-backed party in the absence of any viable opposition.
Thailand will be the fourth country Min Aung Hlaing has visited as president following official trips to China, India and Laos. He will meet Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul on Thursday, before both attend a Thailand-Myanmar business forum.
FINE LINE BETWEEN ENGAGEMENT AND ENDORSEMENT
Anutin said on Tuesday that Thailand's policy was "calibrated re-engagement" to keep channels open with Myanmar and push for its compliance with the terms of a stalled Asean-led peace initiative, a key condition in normalising its ties with the bloc.
Min Aung Hlaing as president has stressed his top priority is peace. However, Myanmar's military has since sharply escalated attacks on civilians including an intensified aerial bombing campaign, a conflict monitor said last week.
While Thailand's approach could strengthen its influence within Asean, it needs to avoid appearing to legitimise Min Aung Hlaing when there is no progress on Asean's peace plan, analysts say.
"What Thailand gains is a stronger role within Asean as a bridge between Myanmar's new government and Asean," said Dulyapak Preecharush, a Southeast Asia expert at Bangkok's Thammasat University.
"There is a fine line between re-engaging and endorsing Min Aung Hlaing's legitimacy."
On Monday, Myanmar's government allowed Suu Kyi, who has been detained since the coup, to meet a representative of the International Committee of the Red Cross after years of uncertainty over her health, wellbeing and whereabouts, a move Dulyapak said could support Thailand's argument for that engagement.
KEY INVESTOR
Min Aung Hlaing's visit also comes as Thailand seeks to revive its economic ties with resource-rich Myanmar, with Thursday's business forum expected to focus on trade and investment.
With investments in industries that include hotels, banking and manufacturing, Thailand is among the top foreign investors in Myanmar, ranking alongside Singapore and China as its primary sources of foreign capital as of late 2025.
Thailand's biggest footprint is in energy, a sector that accounts for nearly a quarter of foreign investment in Myanmar, with Thai energy major PTT Exploration and Production operating two of Myanmar's most important offshore gas fields, Yadana and Zawtika.
Thailand's trade surplus with Myanmar has narrowed sharply since the pandemic and the 2021 coup, with a steep decline in Thai exports while imports - predominantly natural gas - remained steady, according to Kich Aungvitulsatit, chairman of the Thai-Myanmar Business Council.
Thai exports to Myanmar were worth about 67 billion baht (US$2.02 billion) in the first five months of this year, Kich said, compared with more than 800 billion baht annually before the pandemic, with exports squeezed by Naypyitaw's tighter forex controls and the impact of civil war on border trade.
"I see Min Aung Hlaing's visit as more of a gesture of goodwill," Kich said. "It is not likely to have a major direct economic impact." — REUTERS
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: How a pilot who tested positive for drugs bypassed aviation's safety nets
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR:  He was known within the industry as  "a man with a temperament", yet met every technical requirement to fly a commercial aircraft.
That is the profile of the Malaysia Airlines pilot arrested in Indonesia for allegedly attempting to smuggle more than 70,000 ecstasy pills.
Following his arrest, a urine test conducted by Indonesian authorities found  the suspect positive for methamphetamine, MDMA  and cocaine.
The case has exposed what industry insiders describe as a critical gap in aviation safety — a system focused on technical proficiency but with limited psychological screening and mental wellness safeguards.
Speaking to the
New Straits Times
on condition of anonymity, a veteran pilot and industry insider said the pilot's temperament had been noted during his training and career progression, but the system was not designed to flag personality concerns as long as technical standards were met.
"You cannot categorise him as 'bad' because if he was, he wouldn't have passed," the source said.
"He had to be an 'okay pilot' technically to complete the training.
"There is no provision during training to include personal remarks.
"The assessment is based solely on whether the pilot can perform the required tasks."
The insider said  despite the high-pressure nature of the profession, there are no formal peer-reporting mechanisms or structured wellness programmes to monitor the mental health of flight crew.
According to the source, the only psychological assessment pilots receive is an informal conversation during their annual medical examination.
"There is no programme for that. There is no psychological assessment.
"We undergo a medical examination every year and the closest thing is the doctor asking, 'How are you? You okay?' If you respond normally, there is no reason for suspicion.
"There is also no specific section in the official forms assessing a pilot's mental fitness," he added.
He said pilots were permitted to take medical leave for mental health reasons, but an entrenched workplace culture discouraged them from doing so.
"It is allowed, but who will do it? Especially with Asian work culture. It makes you look bad," he said.
While the criminal investigation into the alleged drug smuggling is ongoing, the captain said investigators should also examine the pilot's personal circumstances, including financial pressures or family problems, to understand what may have led to the incident.
"One should look into whether there were financial problems, a sick family member or a need for money.
"We don't know his story yet or what a person might do to help their family."
At press time, Malaysia Airlines has not responded to the
New Straits Times
' request for comment.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Pilot arrest puts KLIA, MAS security procedures under scrutiny
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR:  Senior pilots are demanding to know how a Malaysia Airlines pilot breached multiple layers of security screening at Kuala Lumpur International Airport before being arrested in Indonesia over an alleged attempt to smuggle 25kg of ecstasy pills.
They say Malaysia Airports Holdings Bhd, airport security operators and aviation regulators must explain where the security chain broke down and whether  screening and crew processing procedures were properly followed.
"The question is not whether the system exists. It does. The question is how the bag got through despite multiple layers of security," said Datuk Captain Nik Ahmad Huzlan Nik Hussain, a former Malaysia Airlines chief pilot with more than 17,000 flying hours.
Among  key questions, he said, was whether the pilot underwent the prescribed crew screening process at KLIA, whether his baggage passed through the designated security lane or whether there was any opportunity to bypass standard procedures.
"If the screening equipment at KLIA and Jakarta is of a comparable standard, investigators must determine whether the difference lay in the technology or  how the images were interpreted."
Nik Huzlan also questioned whether the expedited processing of flight crew might have led to reduced vigilance.
"Crew are processed differently to ensure they reach the aircraft on time. That expediency must never come at the expense of vigilance."
[[nid:1505055]]
He said criminal syndicates had, on occasion, exploited airline crew elsewhere because of their privileged access to secure airport areas, reinforcing the need for rigorous and unpredictable crew screening.
Nik Huzlan cited the 2019 Garuda Indonesia case, in which Customs officers intercepted a Harley-Davidson motorcycle and Brompton bicycles transported aboard a newly delivered aircraft, as an example of aviation personnel being implicated in smuggling operations.
The flight's operational profile has also drawn scrutiny.
"If the pilot was serving as a supernumerary safety co-pilot on a training flight, the operating captains and cabin crew who interacted with him before departure might be able to establish whether he displayed unusual behaviour or signs of impairment."
Attention has also turned to Malaysia Airlines' internal oversight mechanisms.
Pilots said the airline maintained comprehensive recruitment, training, simulator, line check and recurrent assessment records, which, together with feedback from colleagues who had flown with the pilot, could  establish whether any behavioural or operational concerns had previously surfaced.
The incident  also prompted calls for a review of recruitment and behavioural assessment processes and pilots acknowledged that human factors were among the most difficult risks to detect.
While stressing that aviation security already relied on multiple layers of protection, pilots warned that organised criminal groups continuously study  procedures for weaknesses.
"If organised syndicates  found a way to exploit a predictable system once, they will try  again. Random checks are the strongest deterrent," said another pilot, who spoke to the
New Straits Times
on condition of anonymity.
He said more frequent, unscheduled random screening of flight crew should be considered  to complement existing security protocols.
Another veteran pilot and industry insider also questioned the effectiveness of the current drug-testing regime, saying scheduled annual medical examinations were no longer sufficient to detect modern synthetic drugs.
He said the demands of the profession could drive some pilots to use stimulants.
"It is quite possible some are hooked to help stay awake and stay focused," he said.
He claimed drugs such as MDMA could leave the body quickly enough to evade routine annual medical examinations.
"Scheduled testing is predictable. Without unscheduled and more frequent drug screening, these drugs are far more difficult to detect."
He said the case should prompt the aviation industry to consider random, unannounced drug screening to strengthen deterrence and enhance flight safety.

Title: US cyclosporiasis probe linked to lettuce widens to 15 states
Article:
WASHINGTON: US health authorities have widened their probe into a cyclosporiasis outbreak tied to iceberg lettuce from central Mexico after detecting cases in six additional states, raising the total to 15 states, the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) and Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) said on Wednesday.
The newly linked states are Missouri, Arkansas, Iowa, Nebraska, New Hampshire and North Carolina, the source said.
Quick service restaurant chain Salad and Go filed for bankruptcy on Tuesday, saying in a filing that it is closing down more than 70 of its remaining locations and citing the cyclospora outbreak as a factor, along with rising petrol prices and reduced consumer spending.
US cyclosporiasis cases have climbed to record levels this year with the current outbreak among the largest caused by foodborne illness in recent US history and health authorities continuing to look for sources of the illness beyond iceberg lettuce. The total case count associated with this multistate outbreak is now 6,358 illnesses reported from 15 states with at least 278 hospitalisations, CDC and FDA said. The agencies' surveillance lags state reporting by several weeks. The FDA and the CDC first identified an outbreak in five states related to lettuce eaten at Yum Brands' Taco Bell restaurants. They later named Taylor Farms in central Mexico as the source of the lettuce. On July 24, they widened the number of states in the outbreak to nine.
Cyclosporiasis can be contracted by consuming food — typically raw fruits and vegetables — or water contaminated with faeces and can cause diarrhoea, nausea and other gastrointestinal symptoms. The worst of the outbreak has occurred in Michigan, where cases have ballooned since June and the state reported the first two deaths associated with the outbreak. It said both individuals had significant underlying health conditions. Separately, Mexico's health ministry said it is investigating the tourist hub of Quintana Roo after British health authorities reported cases of cyclosporiasis in travellers who had stayed there.
RESTAURANT FOOTFALL DROPS
US consumers have been buying less lettuce and avoiding some restaurant chains as the outbreak raises concerns about food safety.
Foot traffic at Taco Bell has declined every day since July 13 except on July 28, when the chain ran a promotional event. Visits were down 11.1 per cent on Aug 1 compared with the average for Saturdays between Jan 1 and July 6, compared to a 19.1 per cent fall the week prior, according to Placer.ai data. Salad and Go has been closing down its locations since September 2025, exacerbated by high overhead costs and ongoing liquidity challenges, it said in the filing. At its peak, the company operated 146 total locations across Arizona, Nevada, Texas and Oklahoma.
The company said it is not alone in its financial struggles caused by the cyclospora outbreak, citing a report saying foot traffic at some of its competitors was reduced by between 3.15 per cent and 11.5 per cent. "In the fast-casual dining industry, which operates on very tight margins, a drop in sales by that percentage is devastating."
Cases have risen steadily across the United States in recent months, according to the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, with reports from 47 states, as the CDC is investigating multiple clusters of cyclospora cases, including one multistate outbreak linked to iceberg lettuce.
Michigan health officials reported 12,218 cases linked to an outbreak of cyclosporiasis on Wednesday, an increase of 710 cases since its last update a day earlier. The state also reported 193 hospitalisations as of July 30.
A spokesperson for the Arkansas state health department also confirmed that it is one of the six new states the CDC is adding to the multistate outbreak. Arkansas has seen 205 cases of the infection as of Wednesday.
North Carolina has reported 149 new cases since July 28 with nine new hospitalisations, according to state health department data.
"Exposures to Taco Bell or lettuce make up a small proportion of the overall increase in cyclosporiasis cases seen in North Carolina over recent months," the North Carolina state health department said in a statement, adding that a fall in new cases suggests the primary sources of exposure have already passed through the food chain. — REUTERS
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Pilots' chief calls pilot's arrest a 'double embarrassment' for Malaysia Airlines [WATCH]
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Pilots Association is deeply embarrassed about the arrest of a Malaysia Airlines pilot in Indonesia for allegedly attempting to smuggle 25kg of ecstasy pills into the republic.
Its president, Captain Ab Manan Mansor, said the involvement of a crew member from the national carrier was a "double embarrassment".
"I'm a Malaysian pilot and I feel very, very embarrassed about this," he said.
"Coming from the national airline is a double embarrassment. Where do I put my face?"
Manan called  for stricter measures to prevent a recurrence and said airlines must  monitor employees for unusual behaviour and conduct random urine tests across the board.
"I think the airline should strengthen these controls and extend them to all staff, including ground personnel at the airport."
[[nid:1505084]]
Manan also questioned the pilot's career progression, as he was still a second officer with two bars at the age of 39.
He said Malaysia Airlines pilots  typically  reach the rank of captain, or four bars, by  30.
Manan also said the government should take a firm stance on the matter as such incidents not only tarnished the aviation industry and the nation's image, but also ruined lives and families.
"The transport minister  should make a statement. The airline also has not  issued a statement on the incident or say if it would strengthen  security measures through random urine tests."
The Malaysia Airlines pilot was arrested by Indonesian authorities at Soekarno-Hatta International Airport on July 28 after Customs officers allegedly found 15 packets with 70,114 ecstasy pills concealed in his luggage.
The drugs are estimated to be worth about RM45 million based on Indonesian market prices. The pilot also tested positive for methamphetamine, MDMA and cocaine.
At press time, Malaysia Airlines has not responded to the
New Straits Times
' request for comment.

Title: Faced with a teleprompter glitch, Canada's Carney mocks Trump
Article:
TORONTO: When his teleprompter malfunctioned on Wednesday in the middle of a news conference on housing policy, Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney smiled and took a swift jab at US President Donald Trump, saying, "I do not view this as a conspiracy."
Carney's remark was an apparent reference to Trump's demands for an investigation after he encountered a halted escalator and a non-functioning teleprompter last year at the United Nations General Assembly, where he delivered a speech.
"I would like to inform you that the teleprompter has ceased to function. Unlike a certain world leader, I do not view this as a conspiracy," Carney said to laughs at the news conference in Toronto.
Carney's office and the White House did not immediately respond to requests for comment.
Relations between Canada and the US have been fraught since Trump returned to the White House last year, slapping broad tariffs on the northern neighbour and calling for it to become the 51st US state.
Carney, who has said he would fight Trump's trade policies, has worked to lessen Canada's diplomatic and economic dependency on the US. He also drew international attention for declaring the end of a rules-based global order and criticising great powers for using "economic integration as weapons."
— REUTERS

Title: Lorry skids near railway tracks: Shuttle Selatan, ETS service delayed
Article:
JOHOR BAHRU: Shuttle Selatan and Electric Train Service (ETS) operations on the Kulai–Kempas route were disrupted today after a lorry carrying flammable liquid skidded near the tracks, triggering a power outage.
Keretapi Tanah Melayu Berhad (KTMB) said on Facebook that train operations were affected while cleanup work and repairs to restore the power supply were underway.
"For affected ETS passengers, shuttle bus services will be provided at Kulai, Kempas Baru, and JB Sentral stations," KTMB said.
It added that Shuttle Selatan passengers should use alternative transport for now, with fare adjustments provided to those affected.
As of 10.37pm, KTMB said train ETS9449 was running 32 minutes behind schedule while ETS9533 was delayed by 55 minutes, subject to operational conditions.
KTMB apologised for the inconvenience and advised passengers needing further assistance to contact station staff on duty.
– BERNAMA

Title: KL gazettes 9 more open spaces to protect green areas

Title: Penang to inspect all heritage buildings after wall collapse
Article:
Your browser does not support the audio element.
GEORGE TOWN: Penang will assess the structural safety of all heritage buildings after a wall collapsed in Lebuh Armenian on Tuesday, injuring two Sri Lankan tourists.
State Local Government and Town and Country Planning Committee chairman H'ng Mooi Lye said the state government would ask the Heritage Department to conduct a study and appoint an independent engineer to identify unsafe buildings.
"Once the findings are available, the Penang Island City Council can issue notices to building owners to carry out remedial works."
The Sri Lankan tourists were injured when stones and timber from a first-floor beam of a heritage building fell on them. They were taken to Penang Hospital for further treatment.
Initial checks revealed that a termite-damaged wooden beam triggered the collapse.
H'ng acknowledged that restoration works often required original materials but there should be flexibility where safety was concerned.
"Sometimes the original materials, such as wood, are no longer suitable. In such cases, alternative materials can be used to ensure public safety while preserving the original appearance."
Lebuh Armenian is one of George Town's oldest and most vibrant streets.
As part of George Town's Unesco World Heritage Site, it is a major attraction known for its rich cultural heritage and well-preserved shophouses.

Title: US cooling firm to build US$150m plant in Nilai
Article:
Your browser does not support the audio element.
KUALA LUMPUR: US-based sustainable cooling solutions provider BAC will invest US$150 million to establish a new manufacturing plant in Nilai, Negri Sembilan.
The Malaysian Investment Development Authority (Mida) said the investment is expected to create up to 200 high-skilled jobs by 2035, including engineering and professional roles.
The project was marked by a groundbreaking ceremony yesterday, attended by Mida deputy chief executive officer (Investment Development) Zuaida Abdullah, BAC president Don Fetzer and BAC global vice-president and Asia-Pacific head Ted Lim.
(0:52) It will be developed in two phases on a 7.36ha site.
Phase one, targeted for completion by the end of 2027, will comprise a 30,000- square-metre manufacturing facility and a regional engineering office.
Phase two will establish a research and development centre and introduce advanced manufacturing technologies, with the core manufacturing facility expected to be fully completed by 2030.
Mida said the Nilai facility will house BAC's climate-controlled product development and testing laboratory in the Asia-Pacific region.
"The laboratory will enable local engineering teams to develop and test cooling technologies for tropical climates and high-density applications.
"Combined with Malaysia's skilled workforce, this will strengthen BAC's regional engineering capabilities and support product innovation," it said.
Zuaida said the investment highlights Malaysia's appeal for high-value manufacturing while advancing the New Industrial Master Plan 2030 and the National Energy Transition Roadmap.

Title: N. Korea warns of 'military options'
Article:
Your browser does not support the audio element.
SEOUL: The powerful sister of North Korean leader Kim Jong-un yesterday accused Japan of "transformation into a war state" as Tokyo beefs up its military stance in the Pacific.
Japan has been gradually moving away from its post-World War 2 pacifist status — increasing military spending, ramping up defence pacts and deploying missile launchers to its outer islands.
Tokyo's defence minister said on Tuesday the military needs to be boosted with a "sense of urgency and crisis", as a new government assessment warned of growing threats from China, Russia and North Korea.
In a statement carried by North Korean state media, Kim Yo-jong said Pyongyang's "leadership will set up additional military options which are obviously due to Japan's transformation".
"Japan, a war criminal state, is accelerating its transformation into a war state," said her statement published by the Korean Central News Agency.
Kim cited Tokyo's recent test-firing of Tomahawk long-range cruise missiles and its May participation in United States-led drills in the Philippines as evidence of Washington's support for "dangerous military moves" in the Pacific.
Tokyo is moving "to formulate the possession of the capability for preemptive attack", she said.
"We will never remain a passive onlooker to the military evolution of Japan which may pose a grave threat."
Japan occupied all of Korea before its 1945 surrender in the Second World War, after which the peninsula was divided into separate states along the 38th parallel.
The legacy of the violent colonial period continues to weigh on the foreign policies of both North and South Korea.
Japan raised its military expenditure by 9.7 per cent to US$62.2 billion last year — equivalent to 1.4 per cent of GDP, its highest share since 1958.
China — a key ally of North Korea — has also recently expressed alarm at what it sees as "new militarism" by Japan.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: South Korea police raid Starbucks HQ over 'Tank Day' controversy
Article:
SEOUL: South Korean police raided the Starbucks national headquarters Wednesday, the chain's local operator told AFP, following allegations an advertising campaign defamed activists slain in 1980 pro-democracy protests.
Starbucks Korea caused an uproar this year when it launched a "Tank Day" promotion on May 18, touting a new line of capacious tumblers for its coffee beverages.
The date marked the anniversary of the 1980 Gwangju pro-democracy uprising, when at least 165 civilians were killed as a military dictatorship rolled tanks out onto the streets.
The chain was accused of trivialising the nation's landmark protest movement and insulting the dead, remembered as martyrs by many South Koreans.
A civic group and bereaved families filed a complaint accusing members of the Shinsegae Group, which operates Starbucks Korea, of defaming and insulting the victims and relatives.
"The Seoul police raided the headquarters of Starbucks Korea this morning as part of the ongoing investigation," a Shinsegae Group spokesman told AFP, declining to provide further details.
Starbucks Korea said in a statement: "We can confirm that an investigative authority conducted a search and seizure today. We understand this to be part of an ongoing investigation."
Seoul police said an investigation into the firm was ongoing, but also declined to provide further information about the case.
The complaint named Shinsegae Group chairman Chung Yong-jin and Son Jung-hyun – the former CEO of Starbucks Korea, who resigned over the furore.
The advertising fiasco also alluded to phrases which officials at the time used to dismiss allegations they had tortured a student activist to death.
- PUBLIC APOLOGY -
South Korea is the third-largest market for the coffee giant, behind the United States where it was founded, and China.
The controversy prompted a public apology and the one-off early closure of the chain's more than 2,000 stores nationwide for staff education in June.
The Shinsegae Group has previously said its own internal investigation found no evidence of intentional wrongdoing.
But it admitted its audit suffered from limitations, such as the executive in charge of planning the campaign refusing to surrender their mobile phone.
Police investigators are hunting for evidence which was not included in the company's own investigation, according to the Yonhap News Agency and national broadcaster KBS.
The so-called Tank Day controversy led to a "sharp decline in sales" in the early days of the scandal, according to the Shinsegae Group.
Starbucks' estimated credit and debit card payment volume fell 17 per cent from May to June, according to local data platform firm IGAWorks.--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Four men stabbed in London, woman arrested
Article:
LONDON: A woman was arrested after four men were stabbed Wednesday in Covent Garden, a busy central London area popular with tourists, in a suspected "mental health related incident", police said.
The 47-year-old woman was detained on suspicion of possessing an offensive weapon and assault following the stabbings shortly before 12.30pm local time (1130 GMT), according to London's Metropolitan Police.
She remained in custody Wednesday afternoon, it said, noting officers had seized a pair of scissors at the scene.
The four victims – aged 34, 39, 42, and 52 – were taken to hospital where two remained with injuries not "believed to be life-threatening or life changing," the force added. The two other men attacked were discharged within hours.
"While still at an early stage of the investigation, we would like to reassure the community that we currently believe this to be an isolated mental health related incident," Met Chief Superintendent Jason Stewart said in a brief statement.
Witnesses working in a nearby restaurant said police had used tasers to arrest the woman, who was known locally as a homeless person who regularly frequented the area.
"They (police officers) were chasing away the lady who had a knife in her hand," waiter Ahmad – who declined to give his surname – told AFP.
"I saw the lady get tased (tasered) by the police, it was the only way they could get her to drop the knife."
Police did not confirm the use of tasers in their statements.
The Covent Garden street where the incident unfolded, lined with stores and outdoor seating, was cordoned off with police tape for several hours.
Striking images published by media showed an air ambulance helicopter in nearby Trafalgar Square.
Another witness, waiter Arjan, said staff saw the confused aftermath of the stabbings, noting "even the victims, they didn't believe what was happening."
"We saw people lying down and the police arrived immediately," he said.
"We know the lady. I don't know her name but she is always on this street, she was homeless and never wore shoes."--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Israel resumes Lebanon strikes amid Rome ceasefire talks
Article:
JERUSALEM: Israel's military resumed strikes in southern Lebanon on Wednesday despite ongoing talks, blaming a ceasefire violation by Hizbollah as state media reported at least one person killed.
The fresh strikes, accompanied by the first evacuation warning in weeks, came as the United States led diplomacy between Israel and Lebanon in Rome aimed at putting an end to hostilities, with Beirut seeking Israel's phased withdrawal from the south.
"In response to a blatant violation of the ceasefire by the Hizbollah, the IDF has begun conducting precise strikes in southern Lebanon," the military said in a statement, shortly after telling residents to evacuate the town of Mansouri in the south.
Lebanese state media said one person died and 11 were wounded in a separate strike.
In Rome, Israel requested that the day's talks with Lebanon end three hours early, a source in the negotiations told AFP, saying the head of the Israeli delegation, US ambassador Yechiel Leiter, had blamed alleged "misleading leaks" by the Lebanese side.
But the talks were expected to resume on Thursday for a third and final day.
In previous US-sponsored talks in June, Israel and Lebanon agreed to a framework deal that involves the disarmament of Hizbollah, a gradual withdrawal of Israeli forces from Lebanon's south and the deployment of the Lebanese army to the region, starting in test areas known as "pilot zones."
This week's negotiations are the seventh round since Hizbollah drew Lebanon into the Middle East war in March with rocket fire at Israel in support of its backer Iran.
Israel responded with heavy airstrikes and a ground invasion that Lebanon says have killed more than 4,300 people.
In its first such warning since June, the Israeli military on Wednesday told the residents of Mansouri: "In light of Hizbollah's violations of the ceasefire agreement, the Israel Defence Forces are compelled to act against it with force."
"For your safety, you must evacuate your homes immediately and move north," the military's Arabic-language spokeswoman, Ella Waweya, posted on X.
The UN's humanitarian agency had said just the night before that more than 800,000 people displaced by earlier fighting in Lebanon had begun heading back home following the recent lull in violence, though more than 360,000 remained displaced.
- 'SHAME, HUMILIATION' -
The town of Mansouri, located around nine kilometres south of Tyre and 10km north of Israel, and its surroundings were subjected to several Israeli strikes and artillery shelling in recent weeks despite the ceasefire between Hizbollah and Israel that took hold in June.
The town's municipality told residents on June 22 that they could return, but asked them to avoid the part of the town that fell within Israel's so-called "security zone" in southern Lebanon.
The "security zone" designates a strip of territory where Israeli forces continue to operate that runs around 10km deep inside southern Lebanon along its border with Israel.
A US State Department official had told AFP that this week's discussions would "include expanding the pilot zone process, resolving all outstanding border issues, and working on a comprehensive peace and security agreement."
As the delegations met in Rome, Italian Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani spoke with his counterpart from Iran, Hizbollah's main patron, and called on Teheran to halt the group's operations.
Tajani, in a post shortly before the Israeli strikes, voiced hope that the talks would "yield concrete results."
Hizbollah leader Naim Qassem said on Tuesday that the direct negotiations would bring "nothing but shame, humiliation" and successive concessions for Lebanon.
Hizbollah has repeatedly rejected the direct talks and refuses to surrender its weapons.
Violence in Lebanon has decreased since the Lebanon-Israel deal and the signing in June of a preliminary US-Iran agreement on the Middle East conflict.
But Lebanon continued to report intermittent Israeli strikes and shelling, as well as detonations and demolitions in southern villages.
Since the war between Israel and Hizbollah erupted in early March, Israel's military has lost 38 soldiers and one civilian contractor.--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Iran, Oman near Hormuz deal as US remains key obstacle
Article:
TEHERAN: Iran and Oman have agreed a route for ships transiting the Strait of Hormuz and are putting the final touches on arrangements for jointly managing the waterway, Teheran's foreign ministry said Wednesday.
But official sources briefing Iranian media stressed that any reopening of the strait would depend on the United States fulfilling what Teheran sees as its commitment to end its own naval blockade of Iran's ports.
Iran has seized de facto control of the strait, a strategic waterway for global energy trade, since the United States and Israel launched their war against the country on Feb 28.
US President Donald Trump has repeatedly insisted Teheran is keen to do a deal to reopen the route to shipping, but Iran denies this and says it will instead make arrangements with its neighbour across the strait, Oman.
"The geographical coordinates of the route envisaged by the two sides have been agreed upon and, if certain third parties do not obstruct the process, the joint statement of the two countries, containing the main considerations and points of agreement, is also in the final review and drafting stage," spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei said, according to state news agency IRNA.
According to the report, Baqaei told journalists that talks with Oman were moving forward, but that even if an understanding was reached, it would not mean that the strait had become safe for all passing vessels.
"The factors making the Strait of Hormuz insecure still exist on the part of the United States, particularly the naval blockade and other aggressive and threatening actions against Iran and its interests," he said.
Before the war, Hormuz carried around a fifth of the world's oil and LNG exports and prices have repeatedly surged since the dispute over the waterway erupted, piling economic and political pressure on Washington.
After imposing an effective blockade on the strait, Iran has insisted ships take a route that hugs the Iranian coast.
Many vessels have instead chosen to take a southern route, close to Oman on the opposite side of the strait, occasionally coming under fire.
Iran wants to control the strait and charge tolls, powers it did not exercise before the war, a development that would be fiercely opposed by the US.
In what has become a regular pattern, Trump last week threatened to hit Iran "very hard", potentially with attacks against civilian infrastructure, only to pull back, hinting a deal was near.
But Iran's foreign ministry denied negotiations were taking place with Washington.--aFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Netanyahu: Israel did not agree to US-backed Gaza plan
Article:
JERUSALEM: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said that Israel did not agree to the US-backed plan for Gaza, even after receiving assurances that an Israeli pullout would only happen after Hamas disarms.
The group's movement, meanwhile, reiterated its commitment to the roadmap published by US President Donald Trump's Board of Peace last week, which includes provisions for the group to hand over its weapons and an Israeli withdrawal.
In a video posted to his social media accounts on Tuesday night, Netanyahu said Trump's team "believes that they can bring about the disarmament of Hamas and the demilitarisation of Gaza."
"We are checking this. They sent us a draft – we did not agree to it, it is not our draft. We sent our comments," he said.
Speaking at an event Wednesday, Netanyahu, who faces a tough re-election fight in October, said that Trump "is our greatest friend, one of the greatest friends we have had in the White House."
But he added: "I also wish to make clear: Israel's existence is not subject to negotiation."
After Israel voiced objections to the initial roadmap, the Board of Peace met with Netanyahu on Monday, assuring him that the Israeli military would only be required to leave its current positions in Gaza after Hamas's "complete" disarmament.
But pressure has been growing on the premier from the right flank of his ruling coalition, with two far-right ministers requesting a new vote to reject the plan, saying it did not reflect what the cabinet approved.
- 'NO OTHER OPTION' -
The request from Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich and Settlement Minister Orit Strook to hold a new vote should be viewed merely "as a campaign move" to put pressure on Netanyahu, according to Tal Elovits, a researcher at Israeli think tank Molad.
But with Israel and Netanyahu looking increasingly isolated on the international stage, the country has little possibility of tearing up the US-sponsored plan, Elovits added.
"Netanyahu has no other option besides listening to his only friend left in the diplomatic community," he said, referring to Trump.
"Netanyahu is not a very active player here. He's an active player maybe in trying to block some ideas, but Israel is not putting anything on the table."
Hamas spokesman Hazem Qassem on Wednesday reiterated the group's "commitment to what was agreed upon with the mediators and the Board of Peace."
The group called on the Trump administration and Nickolay Mladenov, the Board of Peace's high representative for Gaza, to pressure Israel "to abide by the agreement, so that we can see serious and practical steps taken."
US pressure on Israel to curb attacks in Gaza appears to be yielding results.
Israeli media reported that troops have been instructed to seek authorisation from the army chief for strikes, unless they are in "immediate danger" – a change of policy from previous directives, under which attacks only required approval from the head of the regional command.
Israel's military, when questioned, referred AFP to the "political echelon" for a response.
A spokesperson for Netanyahu declined to comment.
Hamas launched an attack on Israel on Oct 7, 2023, which resulted in the deaths of 1,221 people, according to an AFP tally based on official Israeli figures.
Fighters also took 251 hostages to Gaza.
Israel's retaliatory military campaign in Gaza has killed more than 73,000 people, according to the territory's health ministry, which operates under Hamas authority and whose figures are considered reliable by the United Nations.--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Progressive El-Sayed wins Michigan primary in jolt to Democrats
Article:
DETROIT: The Democratic Party's progressive wing scored a high-profile victory when Abdul El-Sayed won Michigan's US Senate primary, according to media projections on Wednesday, giving its anti-establishment message a boost ahead of November's midterm elections.
El-Sayed, whose message focused on healthcare, the economy and an end to unconditional military aid to Israel, was the first progressive to win a statewide primary in a state that President Donald Trump carried in 2024.
He will face Republican former congressman Mike Rogers in November.
Tuesday's vote, billed as a defining test of the party's direction, became an election-night cliffhanger, with El-Sayed notching a narrow victory over US Representative Haley Stevens, a moderate supported by Democratic leaders and pro-Israel groups.
With 99 per cent of the estimated votes counted as of 10 am ET (1400 GMT) on Wednesday, El-Sayed was leading Stevens 48.5 to 47.5 per cent, according to the Associated Press.
The AP and CNN both called the race for El-Sayed, hours after NBC News did the same.
"Money out of politics. Money in your pocket. Medicare for All," El-Sayed wrote on X early on Wednesday, declaring victory.
The race served as a battleground between progressives and moderates over support for Israel, an issue that has played out in primaries nationwide this year.
But unlike contests in liberal bastions, this was a statewide race in a Midwestern swing state for a seat Democrats must win if they have any hopes of securing a Senate majority in November.
Stevens benefited from tens of millions of dollars in spending by a pro-Israel super PAC, and her supporters argued she was the more electable candidate in the general election.
Analysts had said one significant factor in El-Sayed's favour was that Michigan is home to some of the country's largest Arab American communities, where hostility to Israel runs deep.
The result is likely to be scrutinised by prospective 2028 presidential contenders searching for a message to reconnect with voters after the party's loss to Trump in the 2024 presidential election.
El-Sayed's victory could intensify debate within Democratic ranks over the political appeal of economic populism, anti-establishment campaigning and a tougher approach toward Israel.
[[nid:1505007]]
Tuesday's results are consistent with broader signs of a leftward shift among Democratic voters.
A Reuters/Ipsos poll released on Tuesday found self-described liberal voters now make up 71 per cent of Democrats, up from 55 per cent in 2012, while large majorities said universal healthcare, expanded abortion access and higher taxes on corporations and the wealthy are essential policy positions.
The poll also found deep Democratic skepticism of US support for Israel.
Only 16 per cent of Democrats backed continued military and economic aid to Israel, while 57 per cent opposed it, suggesting El-Sayed's criticism of US policy aligned with views that have become increasingly common within the party.
Voters in Kansas, Michigan, Missouri, Virginia and Washington state also decided on US House candidates in Democratic primaries on Tuesday, including a handful that could determine whether the party retakes the lower chamber.
Four of those races are considered general election toss-ups. In a Lansing-area swing district in Michigan, progressive climate activist William Lawrence won the Democratic nomination after two moderate candidates split the centre-left vote.
Lawrence will face US Representative Tom Barrett in November.
Democratic US Representative Marie Gluesenkamp Perez of Washington and state Senate Republican Leader John Braun advanced to the general election in the state's top-two primary.
The progressive candidate, Brent Hennrich, finished a distant third.
In two Virginia districts expected to be competitive in November, Democrats nominated former U.S. Representative Elaine Luria and Henrico County Commonwealth's Attorney Shannon Taylor.
In Missouri, progressive Democrat Cori Bush failed in her bid to take back her seat from U.S. Representative Wesley Bell in a rematch of 2024.
A pro-Israel super PAC spent more than US$8 million to help oust Bush, a vocal critic of Israel, in 2024 and more than US$3 million this year to keep Bush out of Congress.
Bell is heavily favoured to win in November, as the St. Louis-area district is safely Democratic.

Title: India's Gen Z chooses protest over politics
Article:
INDIA'S  Gen Z Cockroach Janta Party, whose recent protest against exam paper leaks claimed a rare ministerial scalp, has no immediate plans to enter electoral politics, its founder said on Tuesday.
Abhijeet Dipke spearheaded demonstrations that spread nationwide from Delhi, forcing Prime Minister Narendra Modi's education minister to resign, and spotlighting young people's worries about high jobless rates despite rapid economic growth.
"We want to consult Gen Z on the issues they want us to focus on," Dipke said in an interview at his home in the western state of Maharashtra, adding that supporters would meet for two days from yesterday to decide their next steps.
"The purpose will be to form the agenda for the Cockroach Janta Party and discuss how we can take this social movement forward," said Dipke, as he posed for photographs with visitors streaming into his two-storey family home.
He ruled out an immediate move into electoral politics, but said he would consider forming a party if "a majority of the people" wanted it, contesting elections later in response to public demand.
"In India, I don't think that forming a political party is a solution right now," Dipke added. "What India needs is a public movement which will fight to bring back the trust and accountability in all the institutions."
For now, he said, the CJP's focus would be on amplifying the concerns of young Indians, many of whom he said had lost faith in the country's politicians, courts and media.
"It's really important to consult these young people and understand what they actually need," added Dipke, who was recovering from typhoid caught during the sit-in protest in Delhi.
After the 36-day protest, Dipke returned to his home town of Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar, to be greeted by hundreds of supporters carrying bouquets lined up on the floor of his home.
Since his return in June following studies in the United States, Dipke become a sensation after his call to protest against medical exam leaks drew tens of thousands of young people into the streets of Delhi last month.
Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigned on July 25 after tear gas and baton charges failed to break up the protest movement.
In its wake, the government has backed harsher legal penalties against exam leaks and set up a panel to review the examination system.
The high-stakes exams are a gateway to secure jobs for millions of young students, who can spend many years preparing in hopes of eventually securing financial stability for themselves and their families.
Dipke said he did not want to form a political party right away as he feared the government would try to discredit it by launching investigations against its leaders.
He also ruled out supporting any political party, despite efforts by India's opposition to exploit the rare opening offered by the protests against Modi.
Some caution may stem from neighbouring Bangladesh, where a Gen Z party formed after young people ousted long-term leader Sheikh Hasina in 2024, fared poorly in this year's elections.
Analysts say elections next year could offer the first test of young Indians' anger as they cast ballots in the country's most populous state of Uttar Pradesh, as well as in the breadbasket state of Punjab and Modi's home state of Gujarat.
But wider general elections in 2029 could present a bigger risk for Modi if the CJP turns itself into a party, analysts say.
"It is unlikely that this issue will cause significant damage to the BJP in state elections, though it could become a bigger factor by 2029," said political analyst Amitabh Tiwari, referring to the general elections.
"If the CJP forms a party, continues to champion youth issues and maintains its momentum while keeping pressure on the government, it could attract support."
At Dipke's home more than a dozen police stood guard after social media threats against him since he first went viral in May, drawing 22 million Instagram followers for the CJP within days.
But his concern was for the safety of his parents.
"I am worried about my parents, and that is why I am very glad to be at home," Dipke said. "I am hopeful that nothing will happen because I have been provided security by the government."
